title: Change-to-failure map
note: One row per change group. No figure is stated here by hand: every measured value lives in the artifact named in its row, which is why the map quotes numbers nowhere and paths everywhere.

changes.title: The evidence lookback no longer returns the organism's own sleep rows (D2)
changes.what_changed: Belief support is drawn from a lookback that excludes sleep-sourced rows, so a belief cannot be supported by the payload it wrote itself.

failure.note: D2: a belief's support could be self-sourced, and every belief figure recorded before the fix describes that evidence set.

changes.prior_measurement: D2 was specified and demonstrated as a code path; no campaign artifact counts self-sourced support, so the size of the effect on any recorded belief figure is unknown.
changes.mechanism: If part of a belief's support came from its own payload, excluding those rows lowers its support count, which changes which belief wins a contest and therefore every belief-support figure downstream of selection.
changes.falsifier: Run the audit trace on the pinned engine and count surviving beliefs whose support cites a sleep-sourced row. If the count is zero, the fix cannot move any belief figure and this mechanism is false.
observables: share of belief support rows by event_type
changes.decision_if_positive: Re-run the belief-revision comparison with the self-sourcing disqualifier armed, since the defect is material to the measurement.
changes.decision_if_negative: Drop self-sourcing as an explanation for the belief-revision gap and leave the gap unexplained rather than attributed.

changes.title: Ranking rebuilt: relation-family stratification, transition predictiveness, generation alignment
changes.what_changed: Candidates are ordered by transition predictiveness and stratified by relation family instead of by raw frequency, and generation indices are aligned.

failure.note: Gate 13: precision at a fixed budget is flat and low under the count-ranked ordering, and the recorded ceiling is one of its measurements.

changes.prior_measurement: The precision-at-budget and coverage curves were measured at the frozen cap under two allocation rules on the frequency ordering.
changes.mechanism: A ceiling in precision-at-budget is a property of the ordering: any ranking that is not equivalent to count-ranked frequency must produce a different curve, and if world edges surface earlier the ceiling moves without any change to the budget.
changes.falsifier: Recompute precision at every budget under the new ranking. If the curve is the same as the recorded one at every budget, the reordering never reaches the signal and the mechanism is false.
observables: rank of the first world edge
changes.decision_if_positive: Re-measure the ceiling on the pinned engine and treat the ordering basis as the lever for an allocation change.
changes.decision_if_negative: Treat the candidate space, not the ordering, as the binding defect and stop varying the ranking.

changes.title: Layer 1 grounding, conditional-entropy ranking, experiment execution
changes.what_changed: Candidates are grounded to the events that asserted them, ranking gains a conditional-entropy term, and the executor path exists.

failure.note: No held-out prediction gain over the strongest simple baseline, with an interval that crosses zero.

changes.prior_measurement: The held-out comparison was run at the frozen cap and returned no gain; the headroom against the strongest baseline was a task property, not a learner margin.
changes.mechanism: Grounding ties a candidate to the event that asserted it, so a prediction that previously rested on co-occurrence now rests on an assertion; that changes which candidates can be cited as support and therefore what the readout is able to use.
changes.falsifier: Count grounded assertions per cycle on the pinned engine. If candidates carry none, grounding cannot change a prediction and the row is inert at this cap.
observables: held-out nats against the strongest baseline
changes.decision_if_positive: Re-run the held-out comparison with grounding as the named mechanism rather than as an unexplained engine difference.
changes.decision_if_negative: Stop treating internal structure as sufficient evidence for a readout pathway and invest in the pathway instead.

changes.title: Decay and promotion: EIG fix, natural-selection decay, temporal edge decay
changes.what_changed: Temporal edges decay, candidates decay by generation, a promotion loop runs, and the EIG term is fixed.

failure.note: The reference arm dies on 0.12.0: theories reach zero and every series is empty to the end of the run, while the frozen arm stays live throughout.

changes.prior_measurement: The death was measured at 3,000 cycles under the frozen protocol, and the cause was isolated to temporal edge decay by disabling it on the same build.
changes.mechanism: Prediction strength is a count over a source frequency; decaying the numerator while the denominator keeps growing drives strength below the stability threshold, so processes fall and theories follow them to zero.
changes.falsifier: Run the pinned engine with decay enabled for 300 cycles. If live theories stay non-zero throughout, the decay-to-death mechanism does not hold on this build and the recorded death has another cause.

result.note: The falsifier ran on the pinned engine at 300 cycles: no theory survives past cycle 38 and no belief past cycle 113, so the mechanism is not falsified and the recorded death reproduces exactly.

changes.decision_if_positive: Fix the decay rule and confirm it on held-out worlds before any campaign runs on this engine; a campaign on a dead reference arm measures nothing.
changes.decision_if_negative: Treat the 0.12.0 death as a configuration artefact and allow the campaign to use the pinned engine as it stands.

changes.title: Prediction cap raised, structural ranking for loops and anomalies, question closure
changes.what_changed: The admitted prediction budget was raised and loop and anomaly candidates gained structural ranking; contradiction density and question closure changed with them.

failure.note: The acquisition gate failed against a named bound: asserted coverage of the world's edges was a handful at most under the frozen cap.

changes.prior_measurement: Coverage was recorded at the frozen cap, and the ranking study recorded how many of the world's edges the top of the ordering recovers at larger budgets.
changes.mechanism: A raised cap admits more asserted rows per cycle, so coverage can change only if the additional admitted rows include world edges; the recorded distribution says the ordering recovers very few even at several times the budget, so the cap bounds how many rows are in play, not which rows are available.
changes.falsifier: Measure asserted coverage at the new cap on the recorded worlds. If it stays at the pre-change level, raising the cap did not address the acquisition failure.
changes.decision_if_positive: The bound was the cap, and the acquisition experiment becomes retestable on the pinned engine.
changes.decision_if_negative: The candidate space, not the cap, is the binding constraint; keep the acquisition experiment out of the campaign rather than enlarging the budget again.

changes.title: Substrate performance, single-pass selection and candidate caching
changes.what_changed: Substrate reads were made faster, selection was collapsed into one pass, and candidate construction is cached.

failure.note: No recorded failure names the substrate or the number of selection passes.

changes.prior_measurement: The substrate equivalence claim was tested; the caching and single-pass behaviour was not.
changes.mechanism: Caching and a single pass can change results only if the cached candidate set differs from a recomputed one, or if one pass admits a different set than repeated passes did.
changes.falsifier: Run both paths on the same seed and compare the candidate sets and scores. Any difference makes this a behavioural change and moves the row into the campaign.
changes.decision_if_positive: Keep it as a substrate change with no campaign row.
changes.decision_if_negative: Treat it as a behavioural change and add it to the map before any comparison uses this engine.
changes.reason: No recorded failure names it, so it has nothing to move; it exists to be proved behaviour-neutral and then left alone.

changes.title: Active environment dispatcher and world-complexity ladder confirmation
changes.what_changed: The environment is dispatched actively rather than held fixed, and the world-complexity ladder was confirmed on the new path.

failure.note: K1 and K2 read the environment the dispatcher supplies, so a change in what is dispatched changes what they measured.

changes.prior_measurement: Phase K ran before the dispatcher existed, against a fixed environment path.
changes.mechanism: If the dispatcher presents worlds in a different order or at a different complexity than the October harness did, the K1 and K2 comparisons move for a reason that has nothing to do with the organism.
changes.falsifier: Replay the ladder on the pinned engine and compare the world sequence and per-cycle complexity against the recorded one. If they differ, the earlier K figures are not comparable.
changes.decision_if_positive: Treat the earlier K comparisons as invalidated and re-run them rather than re-using the numbers.
changes.decision_if_negative: Treat the dispatcher as presentation-neutral and keep the recorded K figures as the reference.

changes.title: Active inquiry and retention pressure
changes.what_changed: The organism can generate questions when information is missing, and retention pressure is audited.

failure.note: P3 reversed: question generation moved development in the opposite direction from the prediction, well outside the one-item noise floor.

changes.prior_measurement: The reversal was measured on the pre-change build as one of five preregistered mechanism predictions.
changes.mechanism: The reversal says generating more questions made development worse; active inquiry changes when questions are generated, so the rate that produced the reversal is not the rate this engine produces.
changes.falsifier: Measure questions generated per cycle on the pinned engine against the pre-change rate. If the rate is unchanged, the change cannot explain any movement in the P3 direction.
changes.decision_if_positive: Re-run the mechanism contrast with question generation as the named mechanism.
changes.decision_if_negative: Treat the P3 reversal as a property of the architecture rather than of the inquiry layer.

changes.title: RoleCandidate and SchemaCandidate for cross-context reuse
changes.what_changed: Two candidate types were added that abstract over the context a structure was learned in.

failure.note: Q012: role abstraction's dependence on orthogonal context, which the record marks as untested.

changes.prior_measurement: None. Q012 is open and no artifact measures role candidates surviving selection.
changes.mechanism: A role candidate abstracts the context away from the instance, so a structure that survived only inside its origin context could survive outside it; if no role candidate ever survives selection, nothing about reuse has changed.
changes.falsifier: Count role candidates that survive to selection outside their origin context across seeds. If the count is zero, the layer cannot remove the dependence and the mechanism is false.
changes.decision_if_positive: Q012 becomes measurable and the orthogonal-context dependence gets its first direct test.
changes.decision_if_negative: Role abstraction is inert at this cap, and Q012 stays open rather than being answered.

changes.title: sleep.py split into submodules, with memory indexes
changes.what_changed: One module became five and the memory layer gained indexes; the commit claims behaviour is unchanged.

failure.note: Nothing by design: the change claims equivalence, so it has no failure to move.

changes.prior_measurement: The equivalence claim was not checked by anything after the freeze check stopped running.
changes.mechanism: There is none by design. The claim being made is that behaviour is identical, which is a proof obligation rather than a mechanism.
changes.falsifier: Run the frozen engine and the split engine on the same seeds and worlds and compare candidate sets and scores. Any difference means the split changed behaviour, and every comparison against the current engine is then confounded.
changes.decision_if_positive: The current engine may be compared to the frozen reference, and the split is not a campaign row.
changes.decision_if_negative: Fix or revert the split before any campaign measurement, because the reference arm and the candidate arm would differ for a reason nobody recorded.
changes.reason: A behaviour-preserving claim has no failure to move; it must be proved before any comparison uses this engine, not campaigned as an improvement.

changes.title: Acquisition scored on unboosted evidence, with content-sensitive priming
changes.what_changed: Acquisition is scored on evidence that carries no confidence boost, and priming depends on content rather than on a fixed prior.

failure.note: The earned cross-context result was produced on this build, so its latency and prior-application counts are measured on the unboosted basis.

changes.prior_measurement: The cross-context run reported a transfer ratio, cycle counts and prior applications on this build; nothing earlier measures the same quantity.
changes.mechanism: Removing the boost changes what counts as evidence for acquisition, so the latency the result reports is a different quantity from the one the October runs reported and cannot be compared to them without rescoring.
changes.falsifier: Rescore the same run on boosted evidence. If the reported latency and prior-application counts are unchanged, the change did not move the result and the row is inert.
changes.decision_if_positive: The cross-context result is the campaign's reference, and this row fixes exactly what it measures.
changes.decision_if_negative: The result depends on the scoring basis and must not be compared across the change.

changes.title: Candidate supersession and the decay confirmation harness
changes.what_changed: A superseded candidate is kept rather than dropped, and a harness was added to confirm a decay fix on separate seeds.

failure.note: Gate 13 asserted coverage moved across three readings on one seed and world when supersession was amended, and the freeze amendment records the change.

changes.prior_measurement: Three coverage readings were recorded on one seed and world, before and after the amendment.
changes.mechanism: Supersession keeps a candidate alive when a newer one replaces it, so cycles that previously dropped a candidate now retain it, and asserted coverage counts surviving asserted candidates.
changes.falsifier: Measure coverage with supersession disabled. If it returns the pre-amendment figure, supersession is the cause; if it returns the amended figure, something else moved coverage.
changes.decision_if_positive: Every Gate 13 figure recorded before the amendment is described by a named cause rather than an unexplained shift.
changes.decision_if_negative: Supersession is not the cause, and the coverage change must be attributed elsewhere before it is used.

changes.title: Diversity-first admission adopted and withdrawn the same day
changes.what_changed: An admission module was added, then deleted after the two-arm comparison on the engine's own ordering returned no gain.

failure.note: The two-arm comparison returned no gain on this layer, and the adoption was withdrawn.

changes.prior_measurement: The two-arm comparison ran on the engine's own ordering and is the artifact that decided the withdrawal.
changes.mechanism: None remains. The module is gone, so there is no live behaviour for a campaign to test; the only mechanism left is the one that decided the withdrawal.
changes.falsifier: Re-read the two-arm artifact: if the arm had shown a gain, the withdrawal would have been wrong. There is nothing to re-run.
observables: absence of the module from the package
changes.decision_if_positive: Keep the withdrawal and cite the artifact when admission is discussed.
changes.decision_if_negative: Re-open admission only with a new preregistration, not by restoring a module deleted on a measured negative.
changes.reason: The arm no longer exists in the package, so there is no live change to campaign; its result is a decision already taken, recorded in the two-arm artifact.

changes.title: Phase L harness defects fixed, release state documented
changes.what_changed: Four harness defects were corrected and the release state was documented; both are outside the engine.

failure.note: Phase L's measurement, not the engine's behaviour, is what these commits changed.

changes.prior_measurement: Phase L was measured before and after the harness fixes, with the verdict unchanged.
changes.mechanism: The fixes change how Phase L is measured, so they can move a Phase L number without moving the organism; treating them as engine changes would attribute an instrument effect to the subject.
changes.falsifier: Re-run the committed analysis on the frozen Phase L artifacts. If the verdict changes, the harness fix altered the measurement rather than the report.
changes.decision_if_positive: Keep the harness fixes out of the campaign and cite the frozen analysis.
changes.decision_if_negative: The harness fix changed the measurement, and the earlier Phase L readings must be marked incomparable.
changes.reason: Harness and documentation, not engine behaviour; including it in a campaign would attribute an instrument effect to the organism.
